---
title: "CLI"
subtitle: "`recueil` — the API with a shell in front of it"
---

::: {.callout-important}
**Partly implemented.** The commands marked ✓ below are in the tree and tested; the rest report the
phase they arrive in and exit non-zero rather than half-working. This page is the intended command
surface, and the table says which part of it exists.
:::

The CLI is a client of the [REST API](api.qmd) like everything else, with one exception: `recueil
serve` starts the server. It mirrors the API rather than reimplementing it, which means anything you
can do here you can also do from a script, and anything the CLI cannot do the API cannot do either.

Machine-readable output on every command via `--json`, so `jq` is the intended companion.

## Commands

| Command | Does | Phase | In the tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recueil serve` | Start the server | 0 | ✓ |
| `recueil import zotero` | Migrate a Zotero library, with a verification report | 1 | ✓ |
| `recueil import paperless` | Migrate a Paperless-ngx server, with a verification report | 2 | ✓ |
| `recueil import bibtex \| biblatex \| ris \| csl-json` | Bibliographic records from a file | 1 | ✓ |
| `recueil import` — EndNote XML, JabRef groups, Mendeley, CSV | The remaining bulk formats | later | — |
| `recueil export` | BibTeX, BibLaTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS | 1 | ✓ |
| `recueil export` — JSON-LD, CSV, Parquet | The analytics formats | 5 | — |
| `recueil ingest` | Push files or a directory through the pipeline | 2 | ✓ |
| `recueil ingest watch` | Poll every configured source, and any `--folder` given | 2 | ✓ |
| `recueil review` | Work the review queue: list, accept, reject | 2 | ✓ |
| `recueil rules` | Validate a rule set, and dry-run it over a corpus | 2 | ✓ |
| `recueil queue` | List, retry and cancel ingestion jobs | 2 | ✓ |
| `recueil backup` / `restore` | Consistent snapshot and recovery | 1 | ✓ |
| `recueil token` | Create, list and revoke scoped API tokens | 1 | — mint them over the API |
| `recueil job` | List, follow, retry and cancel jobs generally | 1 | — `recueil queue` covers ingestion |
| `recueil check` | Run the verification engine over a scope, or over a pasted reference list | 3 | — |
| `recueil dedup` | File and record deduplication, dry run by default | 3 | — |
| `recueil plugin` | Install, enable, disable, configure, list | 3 | — |
| `recueil graph` | Build edges, run a deep dive, export a network | 5 | — |
| `recueil sr` | Systematic review: search runs, screening, extraction, PRISMA counts | 7 | — |

Sources themselves are configured over the API rather than from the shell:
`POST /api/v1/ingestion/sources` for a watched folder, a WebDAV collection or an IMAP mailbox.
`recueil ingest watch` then polls whatever it finds configured.

## Connecting

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `RECUEIL_URL` | Server base URL. Defaults to `http://localhost:8080` |
| `RECUEIL_TOKEN` | Scoped API token |
| `RECUEIL_PROFILE` | Named profile from `~/.config/recueil/config.toml`, for more than one instance |

Global flags: `--json`, `--quiet`, `--verbose`, `--no-colour`, `--yes` (skip confirmations),
`--dry-run` where the command supports it.

## Examples

The first four exist today. The rest are the intended surface of later phases and are written in the
shape they are meant to take.

Import a Zotero library and get a verification report:

```sh
recueil import zotero ~/Zotero/zotero.sqlite \
  --database ./library.db --storage ./storage --report ./zotero-import
```

Migrate a Paperless-ngx server, rehearsing first:

```sh
recueil import paperless --url https://paperless.example --token "$PAPERLESS_TOKEN" \
  --database ./library.db --storage ./storage --dry-run
```

Run the pipeline over everything a scanner has left on a share, with a rule set:

```sh
recueil ingest watch --rules office.yaml --ocr ocrmypdf --database ./library.db --storage ./storage
```

See what still needs a decision, and why:

```sh
recueil review list --json --database ./library.db --storage ./storage | jq '.entries[].explanation'
```

Audit a reference list that is not in your library — the peer-review deliverable:

```sh
recueil check bibliography --file submitted-references.txt --format markdown > audit.md
```

Parse the list, resolve what can be resolved, and report on what cannot: malformed identifiers, DOIs
that do not resolve, metadata that disagrees with the record, retractions and expressions of
concern, preprints with a published version, and references with no identifier and no match in
Crossref, OpenAlex, PubMed or Semantic Scholar — which is the polite way of saying possibly
fabricated.

Look at what a dedup run would do before it does it:

```sh
recueil dedup records --scope collection:phd --dry-run --json | jq '.merges | length'
```

Refresh a bibliography for a manuscript (today: `recueil export biblatex --search '…'`; the
saved-search selector arrives with the saved-search UI):

```sh
recueil export biblatex --search 'tag:"thesis chapter 3"' --out chapter3.bib
```

Snowball from a seed with a budget:

```sh
recueil graph deep-dive --seed collection:phd --direction both --depth 2 --max-nodes 500
```

Follow a long job:

```sh
recueil job follow --last
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Command or usage error |
| `2` | Authentication or authorisation failure |
| `3` | Server unreachable |
| `4` | Job completed with items routed to the review queue — not a failure, but not unattended success either |
| `5` | Job failed |

Code `4` exists because "flag, never guess" needs a way to say so to a shell script. A cron job that
treats it as success is ignoring the queue it is filling.
